ios.desc:
Aligno is built around one idea: momentum is easier when you’re surrounded by the right people.

Connect with others who are working toward similar goals, building better habits, or pushing themselves to grow. Join groups centered around shared interests and ambitions, share your progress, and stay motivated by seeing others move forward too.

Inside each group you can post updates, share milestones, and connect through group chat to keep conversations and motivation going. Whether you're focused on personal growth, learning something new, improving your mindset, or simply staying consistent, Aligno helps turn shared energy into real momentum.

When people move forward together, progress becomes easier to maintain.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Followers are a bad primitive – I built a group-first social app

quotes.text:
Most social apps are built around follower graphs and broadcast reach. I’ve been experimenting with what happens if groups are the core structure instead.

I built Aligno around that idea: chat, posts, events, and shared boards designed for shared momentum, alongside personal goal tracking.

I’m sure variations of group-based social apps have existed before, but this is my take. The idea came from noticing how hard it can be to find intentional communities of people working toward the same goals — and how motivation and momentum tend to fade as life gets busier.

Currently it’s iOS only. If the idea resonates and feedback is strong, I’ll likely bring it to Android as well.

Curious what builders here think. Looking for honest product critique and edge-case feedback.
